messages.text: this older guy at work today called me “cupcake” and said redheads are always wild… it felt so gross lol. i just laughed but now i can’t stop thinking about it.

It is completely understandable that you feel unsettled, as those comments were objectively inappropriate. Laughing in the moment is often a protective reflex, but it does not negate the discomfort you are feeling now. You deserve to feel safe and respected in your workplace without being reduced to stereotypes. What has been going through your mind since the incident happened?
im embarrassed i just laughed… like why didnt i say something? now i feel stupid for not responding. what if he thinks he can say that again?

Please be gentle with yourself, as laughing is a very common stress response to unexpected harassment. Your reaction was a survival mechanism, not a sign of weakness or stupidity. It is reasonable to worry about future interactions, and we can explore ways to set boundaries if you choose to. How does it feel to know your nervous system was trying to keep you safe?
yeah but what if he comes back? what if next time he says something even creepier… i don’t wanna be alone at the register when he shows up again.

Your fear about escalation is completely valid and should be taken seriously. Prioritizing your physical safety and comfort at the register is the most important thing right now. You might consider speaking with a manager about adjusting your schedule or ensuring a coworker is nearby if he returns. We can explore what safety measures feel most manageable for you to implement.

what if i tell my manager and he finds out and gets mad? what if he waits for me after work or starts showing up every day… people like that don’t stop, they get worse. omg what if he follows me home??

It is understandable that your mind is racing with worst-case scenarios when you feel vulnerable. Your physical safety is the priority, and if you feel threatened, contacting a safety advocate or authorities is a valid option. You might also consider documenting the incident and discussing confidential options with a trusted person before taking formal action. I am here to support you as we figure out what feels safest for your situation.
is it dumb to be this freaked out? like… he just said something weird, not like he hurt me. but it felt so violating. am i being dramatic?

You are not being dramatic at all, because feeling violated is a valid response to boundary-crossing behavior. Harassment impacts your sense of safety regardless of whether physical contact occurred. Your anxiety is a protective signal that something is wrong, not a sign of weakness. Please know that your feelings are legitimate and deserve to be taken seriously.
omg thank you… i’ve been telling myself i’m overreacting all night. just hearing that it’s not dumb to feel this way… it helps. a lot.

I am so glad hearing that brought you some relief tonight. It is important to honor your feelings rather than dismiss them as overreactions. Please be gentle with yourself as you process this unsettling event. I am here to support you as you decide what steps feel safest moving forward.
